content:
Proof Obligations: spec.txt satisfied by semantics.txt

0. Satisfaction Theorem (target of all obligations)

  For every expression e, if e →* n (n ∈ Z), then abs(e) →* m with:
      (i)   m >= 0
      (ii)  m = n     if n >= 0
      (iii) m = -n    if n <  0
  i.e., the rules of semantics.txt discharge properties P1–P3 of spec.txt.

  Obligations O1–O3 establish that "the result of e" is well-defined;
  O4–O6 are the main properties; O7 discharges the corollaries.

---------------------------------------------------------------------

O1  [WELL-DEFINED RESULT]
    The induced interpretation 〚e〛 = n  iff  e →* n  is a total function.
    Depends on: O2.
    Decomposition:
      O1a [NORMAL-FORMS]  If e is irreducible (no e' with e → e'), then e
          is a numeral n. Proof: induction on e; literals are values,
          each compound form has a congruence or computation rule.
      O1b [TERMINATION]  Every e →* some normal form. Proof: structural
          induction with measure |e| (number of nodes); every rule
          strictly decreases |e|.
      O1c [DETERMINISM]  e → e' and e → e'' implies e' = e''.
          Decomposes into:
            O1c-i  Congruence rules are mutually exclusive (each
                   operand position / premise shape is disjoint).
            O1c-ii Congruence and computation rules are disjoint
                   (computation rules fire only on values).
            O1c-iii Computation-rule side conditions are exclusive —
                   uses O2b.
      O1d [WELL-DEFINEDNESS]  From O1a + O1b + O1c: every e has exactly
          one normal form, so 〚·〛 is a total function.

O2  [ARITHMETIC SIDE CONDITIONS]
    The side conditions of (E-ABS-POS)/(E-ABS-NEG) are exhaustive and
    exclusive. Proof: trichotomy of Z.
    Decomposition:
      O2a [EXHAUSTIVENESS]  For all n: n >= 0 or n < 0.
      O2b [EXCLUSIVITY]    For no n: n >= 0 and n < 0.

O3  [CONGRUENCE WELL-FORMEDNESS]
    Reduction preserves expression well-formedness and the fixed
    evaluation order is consistent.
    Decomposition:
      O3a [PRESERVATION]  If e is a well-formed expression and e → e',
          then e' is a well-formed expression (immediate for this
          untyped syntax).
      O3b [ORDER-CONSISTENCY]  (E-ADD-L) requires e2 to be a value and
          (E-ADD-R) requires e1 to be a value; their premises cannot
          both hold (uses O1c-i). Left-to-right order is thereby forced.

O4  [P2 IDENTITY CASE]
    If 〚e〛 = n and n >= 0, then abs(e) →* n.
    Depends on: O1, O2a.
    Decomposition:
      O4a [CONGR-STAR]  Lifting lemma: e →* n implies abs(e) →* abs(n).
          Proof: induction on the derivation of e →* n, applying (E-ABS)
          at each step.
      O4b [RULE-POS]  abs(n) → n is an instance of (E-ABS-POS) under
          side condition n >= 0.
      O4c [COMBINE-POS]  abs(e) →* abs(n) → n by O4a, O4b.

O5  [P3 NEGATION CASE]
    If 〚e〛 = n and n < 0, then abs(e) →* -n.
    Depends on: O1, O2a.
    Decomposition:
      O5a [CONGR-STAR]  Same lifting lemma as O4a (shared).
      O5b [RULE-NEG]  abs(n) → -n is an instance of (E-ABS-NEG) under
          side condition n < 0.
      O5c [NUMERAL-NEG]  -n denotes the numeral of the negated integer
          (meta-level negation on Z maps numerals to numerals).
      O5d [COMBINE-NEG]  abs(e) →* abs(n) → -n by O5a, O5b, O5c.

O6  [P1 NON-NEGATIVITY]
    If 〚e〛 = n, then abs(e) →* m with m >= 0.
    Depends on: O4, O5, O2.
    Decomposition:
      O6a [CASE-POS]  If n >= 0: m = n, and n >= 0 (by O4c).
      O6b [CASE-NEG]  If n < 0: m = -n, and -n > 0 (by O5d; negation of
          a negative integer is positive).
      O6c [CASE-COVER]  The two cases cover all n (by O2a); they are
          disjoint (by O2b), so m >= 0 always.

O7  [COROLLARIES of spec.txt §5]
    Each follows from O4–O6 by specialization.
    Decomposition:
      O7a [C1-ZERO]  abs(0) = 0: instance of O4 with x = 0.
      O7b [C2-SYMMETRY]  abs(x) = abs(-x): case analysis on x using
          O2a; each case by O4/O5 and O5c.
      O7c [C3-DOMINATION]  x <= abs(x): if x >= 0 then equality (O4);
          if x < 0 then abs(x) = -x > 0 > x (O5, O6b).
      O7d [C4-ZERO-IFF]  abs(x) = 0 <=> x = 0: (⟸) O7a; (⟹) contrapositive
          of O5/O6b — if x < 0 then abs(x) = -x > 0.

O8  [SANITY: EXAMPLE DERIVATION]
    The derivation in semantics.txt §5 (abs(- (2 + 3)) →* 5) is a valid
    instance of the rules and of O5. Verification by direct
    construction of the derivation tree; not needed for the theorem,
    included as a cross-check of the rule set.

---------------------------------------------------------------------

Dependency summary:
  O2 ──────────────┐
  O1 (O1a,O1b,O1c) ─┴─> O1d ─> O4, O5 ─> O6 ─> O7
  O3 supports O1c; O8 is an independent check.

Status: all obligations are expected to be discharged by elementary
induction and case analysis on Z; none require auxiliary machinery
beyond the trichotomy of integers (O2).
